plan.disposition: small complexity: plan and architecture reviews run at medium+ only (phase matrix)

findings.finding: Tag matching ignores context: a <link> inside an HTML comment, a <script> string or a <textarea> is also fetched and rewritten; a quoted attribute containing '>' truncates the match; replacement is split/join over the whole document.
findings.suggestion: Single html.replace(LINK_TAG, cb) pass; skip comments/raw-text elements.

findings.finding: Relative @import / url() inside the inlined CSS stay relative and cannot load in the opaque-origin srcdoc.
findings.suggestion: Document the limit in the header comment, or inline one-level @import.

findings.finding: Promise.all over every distinct <link> is unbounded.
findings.suggestion: Cap the number of inlined links (e.g. 20) or limit concurrency.

findings.finding: Loading state returns on every text change: the iframe unmounts for a 'Loading...' frame and remounts, resetting page scripts and scroll.
findings.suggestion: Keep the previous iframe until the new inlined result arrives.

findings.finding: Pop-out button sits inside role=tablist but is not a tab (invalid ARIA).
findings.suggestion: Move the button outside the tablist element.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The sandbox still keeps an opened HTML file away from the project's other files, and inlining only reads stylesheets. — Any relative href with rel containing 'stylesheet' is fetched with no extension check; the body is injected as <style> text into a scripted iframe whose CSP allows img-src https:, so a hostile board.html with <link rel=stylesheet href=".env"> plus a script can read and exfiltrate any project text file up to 1 MB.
findings.suggestion: Restrict inlined hrefs to a .css extension, refuse dotfile segments, add a test that href=.env is never fetched; or correct the 'untrusted' wording.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: mask() is safe over arbitrary HTML up to 1 MB. — MASKED is a lazy scan from every opening token; with a missing closer each start scans to EOF (O(n^2)): '<style'.repeat(150000) freezes the UI thread inside the effect.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a single linear scanner using indexOf; unclosed element masks to EOF; add a perf test.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: Only real <link> elements are rewritten and the replacement is positionally exact. — LINK_TAG ends at the first '>' even inside a quoted attribute; link-shaped text in another tag's attribute is not masked;   over-masks '<style-guide>' / '<title-x>'; an unclosed <script> is left unmasked.
findings.suggestion: Use (?=[\s>/]) instead of   and make LINK_TAG quote-aware, or document as best-effort.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The iframe is always eventually shown. — showFrame stays false until inlineLinkedStyles settles; Promise.all over fetchText has no timeout or abort, so one hung stylesheet request leaves 'Loading...' forever.
findings.suggestion: Per-fetch timeout (~5 s) resolving null; add an AbortController.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The user can never see another file's or project's styles. — Could not break it: sameTarget compares projectId and path; A->B->A is safe; the cancelled flag stops late results; '</style' and media-attribute breakout are neutralised; resolveDocPath clamps '..'.

The escape writes a literal backslash into the CSS (`<\/style`). This is a valid CSS escape for `/`, so rendering is unaffected, but only the literal sequence `</style` (case-insensitive) is escaped. That is actually the only string that terminates a `<style>` element in HTML parsing, so it is safe — however, if the CSS also contains `<!--`/`-->` in certain script-adjacent positions inside `<style>`, legacy parsing quirks exist in some engines. In practice the injected CSP (`script-src 'unsafe-inline'` is scoped to the srcdoc's own CSP) plus opaque origin makes this non-exploitable; noting only so the assumption is deliberate.
findings.suggestion: None required; optionally also escape `<!--` in CSS as defense-in-depth.

findings.finding: A `<link>` tag whose attribute value contains `>` (e.g. `href="a>b.css"`) is truncated at the first `>`, so the href won't match and the link is left as-is — a graceful fallback, not a bug. But a truncated match could theoretically still expose a partial href that resolves inside the project, which is still path-clamped. No exploit path.
findings.suggestion: None needed; the failure mode is "leave unstyled."

findings.finding: When `text` changes, the effect refetches even if the link tags are identical (no memoization on the extracted hrefs). In StrictMode the effect also runs twice, doubling fetches. This is a performance nit, not a correctness issue — `ready` correctly gates on `inlined.source === text && inlined.path === path`, so no stale render is possible.
findings.suggestion: Optionally key the effect on the extracted link hrefs rather than raw `text` to avoid refetching on unrelated edits.

findings.finding: The route glob `/api/external/projects//file` also intercepts the initial HTML file fetch, which is intended, but the test doesn't assert that the CSS request went through the project-file API with a clamped path — the unit tests cover that, so coverage is adequate overall.
findings.suggestion: None.  Regression risk: `HtmlRenderer`'s new props are all optional and default behavior (no projectId/path) matches the old path exactly; `smart-viewer-popout` testid is shared with markdown, and the modal condition now includes html — no removed exports (`buildHtmlSrcDoc` retained). Callers are safe.  Overall: ship-as-is; the only findings are low-severity hardening/refinement notes, and spec acceptance criteria (inline + hold iframe, pop-out, sandbox/CSP unchanged, breakout prevention, root confinement) are all implemented and genuinely tested.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: The cached result and readiness check omit `projectId`. Switching projects while keeping the same HTML text and path immediately renders the previous project’s CSS until the new fetch finishes. This also runs the page’s scripts again when the replacement arrives, violating the requirement to hold the iframe until inlining completes.
findings.suggestion: Include `projectId` in the cached result and readiness comparison.

findings.finding: Replacing every stylesheet link with a bare `<style>` discards its loading conditions. For example, `<link rel="stylesheet" media="print" href="print.css">` now applies print styles to the screen preview. Disabled and alternate stylesheets can likewise become active.
findings.suggestion: Preserve applicable attributes such as `media`, and leave disabled or alternate stylesheets untouched unless their activation behavior is explicitly supported.

findings.finding: The regex scans raw HTML, including JavaScript strings and comments. A script containing `const template = '<link rel="stylesheet" href="mockup.css">';` is rewritten too; multiline fetched CSS can turn that valid JavaScript string into a syntax error and break the page.
findings.suggestion: Identify actual link elements with an HTML parser or tokenizer that respects raw-text elements and comments. Add a regression test containing a link-shaped string inside a script.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The diff implements the basic stylesheet and pop-out flows, but cache identity and HTML replacement behavior need correction before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
